Design review · October 3, 2026

iPhone 12
design review

Space Station Passes already looks cohesive on iPhone 12. Keep the dark palette, sky imagery and prominent next pass. Improve the clarity of reminders and observing controls before adding more visual detail.

iPhone 12 · 390 × 844 ptDark mode onlyXcode 27 · iOS 27 simulatorApp 2.1.0 · build 2429 captures · 3 capture tests passed
PrioritiesAnnotated evidenceProposed conceptsAll capturesValidation & scope

The design holds up at this size

Keep

The pale blue action color is distinct against charcoal surfaces. The sky preview makes the observation tangible. The live location prompt respects the iPhone 12 status area and bottom navigation.

The home screen reflows at accessibility text sizes. Larger text consumes more of the viewport, but the text itself is readable and wraps.

Focus the next pass

Make three answers immediate: When is it? Where do I look? How do I remember? The imagery answers the second question well; the reminder model and technical controls need clearer language.

These are design judgments based on screenshots and source inspection, not findings from a user study. No app behavior was changed.

Recommended order of work

P1 = clarity of a core task. P2 = useful flow or layout improvement. P3 = polish. No release-blocking visual defect was established by this review.

P1
01

Make “Remind me” match the pass on the card

Evidence. The hero places Remind me directly under one pass. Source inspection confirms it requests notification permission for automatic ISS and Tiangong alerts; it does not schedule a local reminder for that displayed pass. The prominent × only hides the prompt. This creates a plausible mismatch between expectation and outcome.

Suggestion. Minimum change: label the action “Enable station alerts” and explain “Automatic alerts for ISS and Tiangong.” Preferred design: provide a pass-specific “Remind me for this pass” action, with automatic station alerts offered separately. Replace the large × with a quiet “Not now” action.

Acceptance check. Show a clear confirmed reminder time after successful OS scheduling; distinguish denied permission and automatic-alert subscription. Preserve the separate alarm_scheduled and station_reminders_enabled conversions.

ObservationHomeView.swift:289–348 · Documentation/Analytics.md
P1
02

Fix creation copy and simplify the alarm

Evidence. The unscheduled fixture says View alarm while its primary action says Schedule alarm. Both creation and viewing reference the same localization key. The screen starts with four orbital events and a three-wheel hours/minutes/seconds picker.

Suggestion. Use separate localized keys for “Set reminder” and “Reminder details.” Default to a practical lead time such as 5 minutes before the first visible moment. Offer At start / 2 min / 5 min / 10 min presets, with exact timing and orbital events under Advanced. Show station, pass date and resulting alert time together.

Acceptance check. Retain exact-second control in Advanced. Handle cases where visibility begins after geometric rise. Keep the sheet present during scheduling and show success or failure before dismissal; the current code dismisses immediately while scheduling continues.

PassAlarmSettingsModalView.swift:35, 160–278, 294–310 · NativeRootView.swift:51–62
P2
03

Teach chart controls without covering the chart

Evidence. The compass-on capture puts a large orientation instruction across the center. The eye button has only an icon; the adjacent controls read Chart and 3D. Their labels convey destinations but leave purpose to discovery.

Suggestion. Show a compact, dismissible orientation hint near the compass control. Explain the eye as “Follow on Lock Screen” when applicable. Add short first-use guidance for the difference between the all-sky chart and immersive 3D view, using adaptive labels when space permits.

Acceptance check. Keep the sky path visible while guidance is shown. Audit effective touch targets, especially the 36 pt bell shortcut and 40 pt location row, for at least 44 × 44 pt including any surrounding hit area. Do not infer hit-area failure from screenshot size alone.

PassView.swift · PassChartControls.swift · ObservationHomeView.swift:177–190, 300–312
P2
04

Make pass comparison faster

Evidence. The scrolled station list shows about two complete rows. Each repeats a large circular chart; dates and durations compete with the artwork. Upcoming rows already show peak elevation but need interpretation.

Suggestion. Try a compact pass row: Today / time, station, visible duration, peak height and a small chart thumbnail. Add a factual descriptor such as “High in the sky” with documented elevation thresholds, avoiding promises about weather or visibility quality. Keep the rich chart in details.

Acceptance check. Compare a compact variant against the current one at 390 pt. Aim for three complete readable rows at standard text size, then allow taller rows for accessibility text. Preserve a reliable route to the full chart and per-pass reminder.

AllPassesView.swift · PassPreviewCell.swift · ObservationPassRow.swift
P2
05

Shorten the path to a usable location

Evidence. The app has two intro pages followed by a separate location prompt. The prompt itself is strong and shows both device location and a city option. The idle chooser says Enter address, while home says Choose a city.

Suggestion. Offer “Find passes near me” from the introduction and keep the replay available later. Use consistent “Search city or address” wording. Consider accepting a selected city directly with visible undo rather than a second generic confirmation alert.

Acceptance check. Verify the keyboard-visible chooser, long place names, resolving state, denied permission and search failure on iPhone 12. These interactions were not exercised in this capture run. Keep location_selected at accepted selection, not at result tapping.

OnboardingView.swift · LocationSettingsView.swift · LocationService.swift
P2
06

Give empty screens a next action

Evidence. The empty alarm screen explains how to use a bell inside a pass, but has no direct route to find one and still displays Edit. The empty forecast offers appropriate alternatives.

Suggestion. Add “Find a pass” to empty alarms and hide Edit until there are reminders. For empty forecasts, consider an explicit refresh/check-again action and the next supported forecast window, without implying that future passes have been calculated.

Acceptance check. Distinguish no results, loading and genuine failures. Keep recovery actions visible at larger text sizes. Add a measured conversion only if its question and boundary are documented first.

AlarmSettingsView.swift · ObservationHomeView.swift:402–486
P3
07

Clarify the time context and protect sky labels

Evidence. The weather badge sits beside the current location while the hero describes a future pass. In the 3D capture, a star label shows through the top-right control. The simulator’s Motion unavailable banner is expected.

Suggestion. Label the existing badge “Weather now”; use “At pass time” only if an actual pass-window forecast is available. Exclude or fade celestial labels beneath toolbar and time-control bounds. Add a subtle solid/dotted/shadow path legend on first use.

Acceptance check. Compare the same frame before and after label exclusion; preserve the selected object’s identity and keep labels legible without reducing their font. Verify live motion guidance on a physical device.

HomeWeatherView.swift · PlanetariumView.swift · ObservationSkyPreview
P3
08

Preserve accessibility while reclaiming space

Evidence. The larger-text home wraps correctly. With weather, part of the large reminder row is below the initial viewport. That is normal scroll behavior, not confirmed clipping. Small upcoming details and icon-only actions merit further checks.

Suggestion. Let decorative preview height reduce at accessibility sizes when needed, while retaining essential direction cues. Keep action text and pass details fully readable; avoid shrinking fonts to retain the default composition.

Acceptance check. Check every actionable row with VoiceOver and the largest accessibility sizes, including scroll reachability and selected states. This review captured accessibility2 for home only; it is not a complete accessibility audit.

Three places to improve first

12

1 · Clarify the reminder

The pass card suggests a reminder for this opportunity. Its implementation enables automatic station alerts. The adjacent × is also visually prominent.

Native view fixture · 390 × 844 pt
12

2 · Make alarm setup intentional

Creation is labeled View alarm. Lead time is a precise wheel rather than a practical default and a few common choices.

Native view fixture · 390 × 844 pt
12

3 · Keep the sky unobstructed

The large compass instruction overlaps the path. The eye icon exposes a useful feature without explaining its purpose in visible text.

A practical implementation sequence

  1. Fix the alarm localization key collision and label the existing station-alert CTA accurately.
  2. Prototype per-pass reminder confirmation and preset lead times; preserve distinct subscription and scheduling semantics.
  3. Refine chart guidance, pass-list density and empty-alarm recovery.
  4. Recheck at 390 × 844, keyboard visible, default and maximum accessibility text, plus VoiceOver. Then check the supported iOS release and motion on a physical iPhone 12.

Measure the changes with existing boundaries

Use accepted alarm_scheduled as the per-pass outcome and station_reminders_enabled for automatic alerts. Compare ordered session-scoped funnels and operation failures; button taps and screen visits are not successful reminders. Keep location conversion at accepted selection. These measurements follow the repository’s analytics catalog; this review adds no telemetry.

Design references

The proposed shorter introduction follows Apple’s guidance to keep onboarding brief and optional. Touch-target checks and reflow follow Apple’s interface and Dynamic Type guidance. These support the recommendations; they do not establish that every current control fails a guideline.
